passage: "Rafiq, the invoices are missing again," I whispered at six, and then fixed it myself before our director's review, saying nothing. The first time, two months back, that felt like kindness. By the third time I noticed Rafiq had stopped double-checking anything, because I always would. That evening I saw that my cover was costing Rafiq the chance to learn, and it was making me a little dishonest with our director. So the next morning I asked Rafiq for ten minutes, laid out the three misses, and we built a checklist together. Then I told the director myself: there had been slips, Rafiq was owning them, and here was the fix. My heart was pounding. The director only asked to see the checklist. Jahnavi

qa.q: What was missing before the director's review?
Why was Jahnavi's heart pounding when talking to the director?
qa.a: Jahnavi was nervous about admitting the earlier slips openly after keeping quiet, yet chose honesty anyway.

qa.q: What could Jahnavi do if Rafiq slips again?
qa.a: Point it out kindly, ask Rafiq to fix it and to tell the director, using the shared checklist.

qa.q: How might Rafiq have felt when Jahnavi laid out the three misses?
qa.a: Rafiq may have felt embarrassed to learn the covering had been noticed, but also glad to get a fair chance to learn.

grounding: The narrator has been covering a junior's mistakes, sees it blocks learning, and coaches the junior while staying honest with the director.

passage:
Leadership coaching note, session three. Client: Samir, 26, team lead at a logistics firm.

Samir arrived tense. He told me that over the past two months he has quietly fixed three of his junior Lakshmi's errors: two wrong delivery addresses and one missed customs form. Each time he corrected it himself and told his boss nothing. "She's new. She's trying so hard. I don't want her to get into trouble."

I asked what Lakshmi has learned from those three errors. He was quiet. "Nothing, I suppose. She doesn't know they happened."

We talked about the difference between shielding someone once and hiding a pattern. He admitted he felt protective, and also worried that his boss would eventually find out and trust neither of them.

Plan he chose: sit with Lakshmi this week, show her the three errors, agree a checking step together, and mention the pattern honestly to his boss, along with the fix. Review next session.

qa.q: How many of Lakshmi's errors had Samir fixed?
qa.a: He had fixed three of her errors.

qa.q: What was Samir feeling about covering for Lakshmi?
qa.a: Samir felt protective of Lakshmi, and also worried his boss would find out and lose trust in them both.

qa.q: What plan did Samir choose, and why is it better than covering?
qa.a: Showing Lakshmi her errors, agreeing a checking step, and telling his boss honestly, so she learns and he stays trustworthy.

qa.q: How might Lakshmi feel when Samir shows her the three errors?
qa.a: Lakshmi may feel embarrassed at first, but also grateful for the chance to learn before it becomes a bigger problem.

grounding: A coach's note shows a team lead who has been covering for his junior's mistakes, who chooses to coach her to own her errors and to stay honest with his boss.

passage:
Friday night.

Divyansh messed up the invoice numbers again. Third time. And for the third time, I stayed late and fixed them before Kaveri ma'am saw.

Why? Because he's twenty-two and terrified of her, and he reminds me of me in my first job. When I was new, a senior girl covered for me once, and I've never forgotten how kind that felt.

But tonight, sitting there at eight with his spreadsheet, I realised something. She covered for me once. Then she showed me the mistake and made me fix it. I learned. Divyansh hasn't learned anything, because he doesn't even know.

And if Kaveri ma'am finds out I've been hiding this, she'll never trust my reports again.

So on Monday: I sit with Divyansh and show him all three. He fixes the next one himself. And I tell Kaveri ma'am there were errors, that I've coached him, and what the new check is.

I'm Usha, not his bodyguard.

qa.q: How many times had Divyansh messed up the invoice numbers?
Why has Usha been covering for Divyansh?
qa.a: Usha feels protective and tender toward Divyansh, who is terrified of the boss and reminds Usha of being new.

qa.q: What does Usha plan to do on Monday, and why is it wise?
qa.a: Show Divyansh his errors so he learns to fix them, and tell Kaveri ma'am honestly with the new check, so the junior grows and Usha stays trustworthy.

qa.q: How might Divyansh see the mistakes he doesn't know about?
qa.a: Divyansh probably thinks his work is fine, since the errors were always fixed before anyone saw them.

grounding: A diary entry shows a senior employee who covers for a junior's mistakes to shield him, and who decides to coach him to own his errors and to stay honest with the boss.
